A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenFly and contain readable main text, Appendices A–K, 11 figures, and 7 tables. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original navigation benchmark results, component ablations, dataset analyses, and experiments on 23 real-world navigation tasks, including Tables 1–2 and 6–7.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised OpenFly-Agent benchmark and ablation scores in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The automatic data-generation pipeline and OpenVLA-based agent retain the same keyframe selection, token merging, FIFO history, and grid pooling procedures. The revised scores are not accompanied by a documented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 100K-trajectory dataset across 18 scenes using Unreal Engine, GTA V, Google Earth, and 3D GS. Appendix K retains the same 23 real-world tasks and comparison of training on OpenFly versus AerialVLN.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Random, Seq2Seq, CMA, AerialVLN, Navid, and NaVila; Table 2 retains the same OpenVLA and component controls. Appendix K retains Navid and NaVila. The newly cited FutureSight-Drive is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported splits, 1,800 test-seen and 1,200 test-unseen trajectories, 20 m success threshold, NE/SR/OSR/SPL metrics, and model settings remain unchanged. Neither the main text nor appendices document a protocol revision explaining the changed scores.

E4.justification: Table 2 revises the evidence for combining keyframe selection and visual token merging: KS + VTM success rises from 18.5% to 33.2%, while the other conditions remain fixed. This changes the reported component effects within an existing ablation; no new ablation conditions, robustness tests, or appendix case studies are added.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and dataset sampling/statistical descriptions. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises OpenFly-Agent's central results. Test-seen (NE, SR, OSR, SPL) changes from (115 m, 18.5%, 50.9%, 12.2%) to (98 m, 33.2%, 63.5%, 22.8%); test-unseen changes from (198 m, 5.1%, 27.3%, 3.5%) to (178 m, 10.7%, 48.9%, 13.3%). Table 2 repeats the revised seen results for KS + VTM. Comparator and appendix scores remain unchanged. These enlarge the reported advantage under unchanged stated settings, without explaining whether the revisions reflect corrections or new runs.

T1.justification: The trajectory-planning notation, algorithmic reasoning, and metric definitions are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about automated data collection, the 100K-trajectory benchmark across 18 scenes, and the superiority of the keyframe-aware agent. Higher tabulated scores do not change these claims' stated scope.

C2.justification: The component explanations, generalization discussion, failure cases, and limitations concerning reconstruction artifacts and onboard deployment remain unchanged. Section 6.3 still describes an SR increase from 12.7% to 18.5%, now inconsistent with Table 2's 33.2%.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information are retained, including Appendix I's encoder, Llama-2 7B backbone, history capacity K=2 and action units, Appendix K's hardware, and the promised release of the toolchain, dataset, and code.

R1.justification: v6 adds FutureSight-Drive: Thinking Visually with Spatio-Temporal CoT for Autonomous Driving as reference 31 in Section 2.2's LLM-driven methods citation list. The remaining references are retained and renumbered, without a substantive expansion of the positioning discussion.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date header and citation numbering change, with minor line reflow in Section 2.2. The prose, terminology, section sequence, and appendix organization otherwise remain essentially verbatim.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their structure and placement. Table 1 has slight column-spacing changes, Table 2 drops the metre suffix from the updated KS + VTM navigation-error cell, and the added reference reflows the bibliography across pages 11–12.

improvement.justification: v5's ablation discussion and Table 2 agree on 18.5% SR; v6 changes the table to 33.2% while leaving that discussion unchanged. The method, settings, and appendices provide no explanation for the score revisions. Higher reported performance and one added citation do not establish a quality gain, while the new inconsistency modestly weakens the coherence of the central empirical account.
